newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market strained, rates higher.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market strained, rates higher.

text.p: The Croatian money market remained strained on Friday and call money rates rose, dealers said.
"The banks' accounts shrank to a low of 226 million, the situation only comparable to that of Valentine's Day when they sank to as low as 250 million kuna," a dealer said.
Fresh trade was put at 31.2 million kuna against 80 million kuna demand.
Call money granted at 10.5 percent as well as at higher rates of 11 and 12 percent accounted for two thirds of fresh trade.
Term loans ranged between 10 and 11 percent for four-day funds and 13 percent for 90-day borrowings.
Banks were busy repaying 35 million kuna in previous loans in expectation of a central bank intervention through an injection of repo funds later today.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled nine million kuna as five banks sought funds to cover their shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
